newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek money rates fall, drachma firms after vote.
newsitem.headline: Greek money rates fall, drachma firms after vote.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards plummeted in early active dealing on an expected liquidity injection from forex inflows following the victory of the socialist party on Sunday's elections, dealers said.
Ecu/drachma fell to 300.50/00 at open from Friday's 301.50/60 in moderate volume but rose to 301.20/30 after profit taking, traders said.

"Depos and forex forwards from one-week to one-year are down 40 basis points in early active dealing," said a foreign bank dealer. "The market expects large forex inflows that will boost liquidity and money rates discount this development."

The combination of the strong drachma policy followed by the Bank of Greece and attractive interest rate differentials lures players into opening short ecu, long drachma positions and enhances drachma liquidity, pulling rates downward, he said.
"The market already factors in a rate cut by the central bank this week," a trader at another foreign bank said.
"Everybody realises the Bank of Greece's current 12.40 intervention overnight bid will be gone soon and rates will adjust accordingly."
All traders agreed that interest rates could fall further if massive forex inflows materialised.
The mark was quoted at 157.85/15 drachmas from Friday's 158.845 fix, the dollar at 239.33/43 drachmas from 240.860 and the Ecu at 300.09/19 from 301.650 drachmas.
